title: Personal Checking: Linked Savings and the Debit That Opened a Negative Episode
content:
## Principle

A Personal Checking extended overdraft fee exists only because a negative episode did. If the debit that opened the episode would have been paid by an overdraft protection transfer, the balance would never have gone negative and no episode would have started; an extended overdraft fee charged on that episode is then a bank error.

## The test applied in the refund decision

Where the debit that opened the episode has been identified, whether a transfer would have paid it is decided on facts read when the refund decision is made:

- the savings account that the checking account names as its overdraft protection link at that time;
- whether that savings account's tier is eligible, under the Savings & Money Market Accounts terms, to act as an overdraft protection source;
- that savings account's current balance at that time, set against the whole amount of the opening debit.

A transfer would have paid the debit when the linked tier is eligible and the current savings balance is at least the whole amount of the debit. This way of judging is confined to the refund decision; the transfers the bank actually makes remain subject to the whole-shortfall condition at the moment of the debit.

## Condition table

| Situation found in the records | Would a transfer have paid the opening debit? | Extended overdraft fee on this ground |
|---|---|---|
| opening debit identified; linked tier eligible; savings holds at least the debit | it would | charged in error |
| opening debit identified; linked tier eligible; savings holds less than the debit | it would not | stands |
| opening debit identified; linked tier not eligible | it would not | stands |
| opening debit not identified | cannot be shown | no finding |

## Hypothetical case

The episode's opening debit was a 640.00 USD check. Today the linked savings account, of an eligible tier, holds 1200.00 USD: the check would have been paid by a transfer, the episode would not have begun, and the extended overdraft fee is a bank error. With 600.00 USD in the savings account instead, this ground finds no error.
